record.context_brief: Sequential Dini property with non-normal cone
record.original_question: Characterize those ordered Banach spaces X whose cone X+ is non-normal but for which every increasing weakly convergent sequence is nevertheless norm convergent.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 6.5. Characterize those ordered Banach spaces X (with non-normal cone) in which every increasing weakly convergent sequence is norm convergent.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X, \|\cdot\|)$ be a real Banach space equipped with a partial order $\le$ induced by a closed convex cone $X_+ \subseteq X$ (i.e., $x \le y$ iff $y - x \in X_+$). The cone $X_+$ is called normal if there exists a constant $C > 0$ such that $0 \le x \le y$ implies $\|x\| \le C\|y\|$. Say that $X$ has the sequential Dini property if every increasing sequence $(x_n)$ in $X$ (meaning $x_n \le x_{n+1}$ for all $n$) that converges weakly converges in norm.

Give an intrinsic characterization of those ordered Banach spaces $X$ whose cone $X_+$ is non-normal but which nevertheless possess the sequential Dini property: every weakly convergent increasing sequence in $X$ is norm convergent.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in a 2024 work on increasing sequences in ordered Banach spaces. Related results show that on reflexive ordered Banach spaces with non-normal cone, Dini-type theorems fail, but no characterization of the non-normal-cone spaces in which weak-to-norm convergence of increasing sequences holds appears to have been published. No solution was located.

status_evidence.title: Increasing sequences in ordered Banach spaces — new theorems and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Dini's theorem never holds on reflexive ordered Banach spaces with non-normal cone; open problems regarding characterization are stated.
status_evidence.claim: The characterization is explicitly listed as an open problem.
